{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMdNDs8AAAABY87vRw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnXy5zhCihjs", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnXy5", "number": 17, "title": "Upgrade Gene Light comparison demo to three-mmd 0.1.2", "body": "## Problem

The Gene Light side-by-side demo in `mmd-gltf` currently uses `@takahirox/three-mmd@0.1.1` to render the **direct PMX reference** (left pane). Upstream [three-mmd-loader](https://github.com/takahirox/three-mmd-loader/blob/main/package.json) now declares **0.1.2**. Update the demo to the released version while preserving the glTF comparison and its reproducible tests.

## Expected outcome

Use `@takahirox/three-mmd@0.1.2` in the direct-PMX side of the public [Gene Light comparison](https://takahirox.github.io/mmd-gltf/). The right-hand converted GLB must continue using the local `MMD_materials_toon` GLTFLoader plugin and its independent PBR fallback.

## Context and reproduction

- Current `mmd-gltf/package.json` pins `@takahirox/three-mmd: "0.1.1"`; update `package-lock.json` consistently.
- The upstream `three-mmd-loader/package.json` declares version `0.1.2` and peer dependency `three: "~0.186.0"`; the demo currently pins `three: "0.186.1"`, which is compatible.
- [`examples/main.ts`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/examples/main.ts) loads the original PMX with `MMDLoader` and the converted GLB with `GLTFLoader` + `MMDToonPlugin`.
- [`docs/comparison.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/mmd-gltf/blob/main/docs/comparison.md) preserves historical screenshots from 0.1.0 and 0.1.1. Retain that history.
- The PMX reference is **not the original MikuMikuDance executable**. Do not interpret differences between the two panes as proof of MMD correctness or modify the glTF extension's normative equations to force a match.

## Implementation

1. Upgrade `@takahirox/three-mmd` to the exact published **0.1.2** in `package.json` and `package-lock.json`; verify that `npm ci` resolves it and that `npm ls three @takahirox/three-mmd` shows one compatible Three.js runtime.
2. Review upstream 0.1.2 changes relevant to the PMX loader, materials, geometry, and rendering. Make only necessary integration changes to the direct-PMX demo; preserve the converted GLB and its loader.
3. Confirm that the two-pane demo still renders the **same Gene Light base pose**, matched geometry/scale, camera, light settings and background. Preserve synchronized orbit/zoom, front/side/back presets, responsive layout, WebGL2, and glTF toon/PBR switching.
4. Capture and **visually inspect** reproducible front/side/back comparison screenshots after the upgrade. Record any significant changes to the direct-PMX appearance relative to the 0.1.1 captures; preserve historical evidence and label version-specific captures clearly.
5. Update all relevant documentation/version references and tests, including any recorded expected appearance changes. Do not change `MMD_materials_toon` spec, converter, color-space rules, or conformance vectors without an independently demonstrated issue requiring a separate scoped change.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] `package.json` and lockfile pin and install `@takahirox/three-mmd@0.1.2` successfully, without duplicate/incompatible Three.js copies.
- [ ] The built example loads the original Gene Light PMX through three-mmd **0.1.2** and the converted GLB through the existing MMD glTF plugin; both views are visible and properly labeled with no asset/network/shader/runtime errors.
- [ ] Matched base pose, scale, camera, navigation, front/side/back views, and glTF toon/PBR switching still work. Attribution, notices, and asset hash checks remain intact.
- [ ] Browser-rendered comparison captures have been inspected for visual regressions, with any necessary compatibility fixes and documented version-related differences.
- [ ] Relevant tests/checks pass: `npm ci`, `npm ls three @takahirox/three-mmd`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:browser`, `npm run check:links`, and `git diff --check`. Record actual results and any justified skips.
- [ ] Changes stay focused on the dependency upgrade, required demo compatibility, tests, and documentation; do not introduce unrelated refactoring or material specification changes.

## Optional validation

Test native WebGPU rendering if a supported adapter is available; lack of an adapter is not a blocker when WebGL2 checks pass.

## Required post-merge verification

After merging to `main` and deploying GitHub Pages, open https://takahirox.github.io/mmd-gltf/ and confirm that both panes render, navigation and glTF toon/PBR switching work, required assets/notices load, and the browser reports no runtime/network errors. Record the deployment workflow and commit. These publication checks occur **after merge**, not as pre-merge gates.
